questions.question: Summarize the discussion on storage disks and computer connections
questions.reference_answer: The participants learned that the storage disks had eventually arrived. They were waiting on the disks to be installed. Grad E volunteered storage space on their own computer for the meantime. The meetings were around 1.5 gigs uncompressed and .5 gigs compressed. So, the group needed substantial space. The professor encouraged the team members to talk to Dave, the person responsible for managing the organization's storage systems, and figure things out.

oracle.answer:
The discussion on storage disks and computer connections revolves around the need for additional storage space and the setup of newly arrived SUN-Blade servers. Grad A mentions that they need more space due to the accumulation of meeting data and transcription tasks. The group discusses the possibility of using the new SUN-Blades for expanding storage, as they have spare drive bays that can accommodate commodity hard drives. However, setting up these blades is delayed because Dave Johnson, who handles such tasks, is away for ten days.

They discuss the cost-effectiveness of purchasing additional disks but recognize the challenge of finding space in the machine room and the need for a direct conversation with Dave to resolve these issues.

The group agrees that a short-term solution might involve temporarily storing data on isolated machines, while a longer-term plan involves discussing with Dave upon his return to address the storage and networking challenges comprehensively.

For general catchup meetings like this, they thought it would make sense to alternate every two weeks. The team joked around about having a guys meeting, as one of the groups would not have any female members. They were mainly concerned with collecting more data through their own meeting recordings. Though, many of the meetings they were having for that purpose were shorter than they would have liked.
